l.i: Ostendunt terris hunc tantum fata nec ultra Esse finunt.

main_text.l: Ioannes Thomas Freigius Rhetoricę secundus à Cęlio filio professor est, minime tamen professionis humanitate contentus, altiorem iurisprudentię facultatem consequutus, pro ętate spem facit ampliorum vigiliarum. Quid Dialecticę professio quantos viros habet? Philippus Bechius studiose & laboriose teneram iuventutem erudiuit, & Pachymerium é græco convertit. Ioan. Fieglinus differendi facultatem in schola sic instituit, ut in sacris concionibus eloquentiam populo admirabilem faciat. Tu vero (mi Ioan. Hospiniane) non solum literis latinis & græcis, sed assiduis in Aristotelis organo vigiliis & editis & meditatis, sed professionis fide, sed officii quadam religione egregiam laudem consequutus es: sed tu tuique professionis hujus collegę cęteri partibus infinitis ampliorem laudem consequemini, si dialecticum ut artificium, sic artificii usum in Virgilio & Homero, in Cicerone & Demosthene iuventuti proponatis, & quotidianę imitationis exeplo & opere informetis: partiamini tempora professionis logicę, minimam tempo-

page.notes: The page number is printed as "2o", with a final o shaped like a zero; transcribed as 20. The catchword "ris par-" completes "tempo-ris par-" and is not repeated in the text. The epigraph is a verse quotation from Virgil, set in italic and printed with "s" and "u" forms, normalised to s and u. The first word "roglyphicorum" is a fragment of "hieroglyphicorum" and stays as printed. Printed "Hofpiniane" and "Pachymerium" are normalised as Hospiniane and Pachymerium. Printed "exeplo" is kept as printed.
